live.name: GOLD HARVEST
live.headline: GOLD HARVEST: a threat actor tracked under several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists GOLD HARVEST under five other names and names three remote-access tools tied to it. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: The catalogue record, sourced to Secureworks, tracks the actor as GOLD HARVEST.
The same record lists these aliases: Octo Tempest, Roasted 0ktapus, Scatter Swine, Scattered Spider and UNC3944.
The record lists three tools: AnyDesk, ConnectWise Control and Logmein.
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: GOLD HARVEST
next.headline: GOLD HARVEST (Scattered Spider): a help-desk social engineering crew behind retail, insurance and airline intrusions
next.in_short: Also tracked as Scattered Spider and Octo Tempest, this financially motivated group is described by vendors as relying on phone and help-desk social engineering. Many attributions to it rest on media reports and circumstantial evidence.

sentences.t: GOLD HARVEST is also tracked as Octo Tempest, Roasted 0ktapus, Scatter Swine, Scattered Spider and UNC3944.
CrowdStrike describes Scattered Spider as a prolific eCrime adversary that has run financially motivated activity since early 2022.
Check Point Research, drawing on public intelligence, describes the group as composed primarily of young people aged 19 to 22 from the US and UK.
Trustwave SpiderLabs says a brand called Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters borrows the names of Scattered Spider, ShinyHunters and LAPSUS$. It reads this as a situational alliance, not a formal merger.
CrowdStrike says early campaigns reportedly hit customer relationship management and business-process outsourcing firms, plus telecommunications and technology companies.
ReliaQuest reports that 70% of the group's targets are in technology, finance and retail trade.

Halcyon says the group compromises call centers and other outsourcing providers to reach many clients. It assesses that attacks on UK retail and US insurance likely began, at least in part, with such compromises.

Check Point says the group is now also targeting aviation. It cites media reports and advisories for the link to airline attacks, and says it found about 500 phishing domains that follow the group's naming patterns, not all confirmed malicious.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group is quoted as saying the group has been going after US insurers. An Aflac spokesperson could not name a group behind its breach, though the report says it shows all the signs of Scattered Spider.
Mandiant says UNC3944 targets IT help desks to get around multifactor authentication.
ReliaQuest says the group relies on phishing, voice phishing and help-desk impersonation, and uses phishing frameworks such as Evilginx to bypass multifactor authentication.
Check Point lists SIM swapping, MFA fatigue ("push bombing") and tricking employees into installing remote access tools among its methods.
Halcyon says the group has consistently used insider recruitment. It also says encryption is typically an escalation step, not the first goal.
The catalogue record lists AnyDesk, ConnectWise Control and Logmein among its tools.
CrowdStrike Intelligence reports that the group used the open-source proxy tool rsocx in activity involving VMware vCenter servers.
ReliaQuest says the group has strategic alliances with ransomware operators ALPHV, RansomHub and DragonForce. Halcyon says it has been linked to Akira, Play, Qilin and DragonForce payloads.
BleepingComputer's report says the group breached MGM Resorts in September 2023 by impersonating an employee, then encrypted over 100 VMware ESXi hypervisors with BlackCat ransomware.

ReliaQuest notes that a May 2025 wave of attacks hit UK retailers including Marks & Spencer, Co-op and Harrods. It says nothing definitive ties them to Scattered Spider, though their coordination hints at a broader campaign.
Resecurity attributes ransomware attacks on WestJet, Hawaiian Airlines and Qantas in mid-2025 to Scattered Spider.

EclecticIQ analysts assess that ShinyHunters is very likely relying on members of Scattered Spider and The Com for voice phishing. The same report says there is no direct relationship between ShinyHunters and Scattered Spider.
ReliaQuest says there is plenty of circumstantial evidence of a deliberate partnership between ShinyHunters and Scattered Spider in a 2025 wave of Salesforce attacks.

Rapid7 investigated an April 2026 intrusion that began with a Microsoft Teams message from a fake IT Support account. It says the approach mirrors Octo Tempest-style tradecraft, and does not call this a confirmed link.
Verify help-desk requests, especially MFA resets, through a second channel the caller does not control.
Treat outsourced support providers as part of your own attack surface and hold them to the same identity controls.
